research_rationale: Executive Order 9941 (March 26, 1948; 13 FR 1625) is a single paragraph that authorizes the Secretary of State to exercise the President's authority under sections 801(a) and 881(a) of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 to prescribe rules for the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System and for deposits of voluntary contributions into the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability Fund. Section 2 of Executive Order 10897 (signed December 2, 1960; 25 FR 12429, from the Federal Register text held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10897.txt) provides that Executive Order No. 9941 "is hereby superseded." Section 3 of that order provides that it "shall be effective as" of "October 16,1960". The order is therefore no longer in force on 2026-10-14. The status of this order was undecided, with no adopted provisional status. It is judged here from the order's own single command, the held text of the superseding order, the Office of the Federal Register disposition note ('Superseded by: EO 10897, December 2, 1960') and the bounded searches, all of which agree. The first end is recorded as the effective date stated in section 3 of Executive Order 10897 (1960-10-16), not its signing date (1960-12-02); a reader who treats the supersession as operative only from signing would date it 1960-12-02. Either date precedes the cutoff.
savings_reason: The authority that Executive Order 9941 delegated is re-delegated to the Secretary of State by section 1(a) and (c) of Executive Order 10897 (sections 801(a) and 881(a) of the Foreign Service Act of 1946), and section 3 of that order lets the Secretary make rules issued under section 1 effective on or after October 16, 1960. Executive Order 9941 created no right, fund or pending proceeding of its own, so nothing survives under this order independently of its successor.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists in the held record. The order is one authorization with no deadline, condition or sunset (own-text signals in the view are text of neighbouring documents on the same Federal Register page, not words of this order). A search of the held order texts for the number 9941 found only Executive Order 10897 (its Federal Register text and an American Presidency Project copy), and Federal Register page texts for Executive Orders 9940 and 10898 that print this order or the superseding section on the same page; no earlier revocation or supersession exists. The Office of the Federal Register note on Executive Order 10897 records that it was later revoked by Executive Order 12292 (February 23, 1981), whose section 10(g) lists Executive Order No. 10897; the held text of Executive Order 12292 does not name Executive Order 9941 and contains no revival, and a revocation of the superseding order does not by itself restore a superseded one, so the supersession of Executive Order 9941 stands.
scope_check: The superseding instrument names Executive Order No. 9941 as a whole, not a part, and the order consists of one operative paragraph, so partial supersession is not at issue. The section 3 effective date applies to Executive Order 10897 as a whole, including its section 2.
independent_command_check: The paragraph contains one command, a delegation of two statutory presidential authorities (sections 801(a) and 881(a) of the Foreign Service Act of 1946) for one purpose, internal management of the Government. Executive Order 10897 sections 1(a) and 1(c) re-delegate the same two authorities, so neither authority is left running under Executive Order 9941. No independent command exists.
savings_check: Savings are recorded as transferred to the successor delegation in Executive Order 10897; see savings reason.

research_rationale: Executive Order 8187 (June 29, 1939; filed June 30, 1939) is a one-sentence amendment of the Civil Service Rules: that Subdivision VI of Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules is amended by adding a paragraph (paragraph 6, excepting FBI positions other than fingerprint classifiers for the period July 1, 1939 to June 30, 1940). Its only command is that self-executing amendment, which was carried out when the order was issued. The order imposes no duty on any officer, sets no deadline for later action and revokes nothing, so no continuing command remained in the order itself after issue. What remained was the inserted paragraph 6 in the Rules, and by its own words that paragraph applied only for a period that began on July 1, 1939 and was "ending June 30, 1940" (recorded inclusively, so the exclusive reading ends the period as June 30, 1940 begins). The order's status was undecided and its status history is the single Office of the Federal Register catalog observation whose note text is empty, which establishes no current effect. The status is therefore judged from the order's own terms and the bounded searches: the order is not in force on 2026-10-14. Searching the held order texts for the paragraph's wording found later orders that re-amended paragraph 6 of Subdivision VI for later one-year periods; they amend the Rules text that this order inserted, not any command of this order, and none names Executive Order 8187 by number (no held text cites that number as a revoked, superseded or extended order).
savings_reason: The only surviving consequence of the order was the inserted paragraph 6 of Subdivision VI of Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules, which by its own words covered only the period beginning July 1, 1939 and ending June 30, 1940. The bounded searches of the U.S. Code, the eCFR and the Office of the Federal Register catalog found no citation of this order, so no right, appointment or pending proceeding under the order is shown to survive into 2026.

An empty note shows neither that the order is in force nor that it ended, and it is not relied on. The status rests on the order's own text, in which the command is a self-executing amendment spent on issue and the inserted paragraph states its own period ending June 30, 1940, and on the three bounded searches, which found no citation of the order."}
earlier_end_check: The order's single command was spent when the order was issued on June 29, 1939, so no earlier end can precede that date; the order is not an amendment of another numbered order and has no condition, deadline or report date. No later instrument is recorded as ending it: the three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Office of the Federal Register catalog) report no hit for this order, and a search of the held order texts for the number 8187 and for the paragraph's wording found no order that revokes, supersedes or extends it by number.
scope_check: The order has one operative sentence and one command, so there is no partial amendment or partly surviving clause to separate. The period stated in the inserted paragraph is a limit on the paragraph's coverage, not a separate command of the order. The inclusive reading of the stated end date is recorded in the savings reason; the exclusive reading changes the paragraph's last day, not the order's first end.
independent_command_check: No independent command exists. The order contains the amending instruction and the inserted paragraph text it quotes; it does not direct any agency to act, report or appoint.
savings_check: No surviving right or obligation is shown. The inserted paragraph's own period ended June 30, 1940, and nothing held shows a right under it that outlived that date.
